From the inflation desk: UK June CPI +2.6% vs +2.7% y/y expected Prior +2.8% UK June core CPI +2.6% vs +2.5% y/y expected Prior +2.6% As expected, UK headline annual inflation eased in June but the real surprise in this report is that core annual inflation came in higher than estimated.

That contrasts with analyst expectations, with some potential downside risks flagged prior the report release even.

In terms of monthly estimates, headline inflation was up only 0.1% on the month but core inflation was seen up 0.3% (vs estimated 0.2%).

Looking at the breakdown, food price inflation was slightly softer on the month (-0.2%) alongside transport (-0.3%).

However, that is more than offset by travel-related spending with prices for restaurants and hotels up 1.0% and recreation and culture up 0.5% on the month.

At the balance, goods price inflation was seen slowing to 1.7% in June - down from 2.0% in May.

Meanwhile, services inflation only eased marginally to 3.6% in June from 3.7% in May.

The latter in particular was estimated to fall to around 3.5%, so that is in some sense hotter than anticipated and contributed to the more stubborn core annual inflation figure.

INFLATION READ: EUROPEAN SESSION In the European session, the only highlight was the UK CPI report.

The data showed headline inflation easing in June due to lower energy prices but core inflation coming higher than expected, matching the prior month's figure.

Overall, the data doesn't change much for the BoE as the majority of policymakers prefer to keep interest rates higher for longer rather than increasing borrowing costs.

The market reaction to the data release was pretty muted.

AMERICAN SESSION In the American session, we don't have anything on the agenda as it's usually the case for Wednesdays.

The focus remains on US-Iran headlines as both sides continue to exchange strikes with no end in sight yet.

This is keeping the risk sentiment on the defensive and such conditions will likely persist until we get a clear de-escalation.

This article was written by Giuseppe Dellamotta at investinglive.com.
